saw.d: a condensed but memorable saying embodying some important fact of experience that is taken as true by many people

sawyer.d: any of several beetles whose larvae bore holes in dead or dying trees especially conifers

saw-like.d: having rough edges that can be used for sawing

sawdust.d: fine particles of wood made by sawing wood

sawtooth.d: a serration on a saw blade

saw-toothed.d: notched like a saw with teeth pointing toward the apex

sawbill.d: large crested fish-eating diving duck having a slender hooked bill with serrated edges

sawmill.d: a mill for dressing logs and lumber

sawm.d: the third pillar of Islam is fasting (primarily during the month of Ramadan); Muslims abstain from food and drink and gambling and all sensuous pleasures from sunrise to sunset during Ramada

sawfly.d: insect whose female has a saw-like ovipositor for inserting eggs into the leaf or stem tissue of a host plant

sawan.d: the fifth month of the Hindu calendar

sawhorse.d: a framework for holding wood that is being sawed

sawbuck.d: a framework for holding wood that is being sawed

sawbones.d: a physician who specializes in surgery

sawpit.d: a pit over which lumber is positioned to be sawed by two men with a long two-handed saw

sawfish.d: primitive ray with sharp teeth on each edge of a long flattened snout

saw log.d: log large enough to be sawed into boards

saw set.d: a tool used to bend each alternate sawtooth at a slight angle outward
